extracted.intended_audience: attorneys and practitioners authorized to practice before the USPTO; Office of Enrollment and Discipline (OED) staff; legal/regulatory professionals handling practitioner discipline
extracted.subtask_description: Final Order under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 imposing reciprocal discipline on a practitioner based on state-court suspension; includes grounds for discipline, applicable regulatory citations, required notifications, and administrative restrictions placed on practice before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may impose reciprocal discipline identical to discipline imposed by a duly constituted authority of a State, pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice and Order pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 was mailed to respondent and provided an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing the imposition of reciprocal discipline identical to that imposed by the state court, based on reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discipline is ordered for violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order states suspension is ordered pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 for violation of § 11.804(h) (as cited in the Order).

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to file a timely response to the Notice and Order (37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) consequence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent did not file a response to the Notice and Order; in light of this failure, there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because respondent failed to file a response within the prescribed period, the Office determined there was no genuine issue of material fact and imposed reciprocal discipline identical to the state's discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to communicate with a client
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent was found to have failed to communicate with a client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This failure was one of the grounds upon which the Minnesota Supreme Court predicated its suspension and is recited in the USPTO's Notice of Suspension published in the Official Gazette.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to hold client funds in trust
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent failed to hold client funds in trust as required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Minnesota Supreme Court's order was predicated in part on failing to hold client funds in trust; the USPTO's reciprocal discipline references this as cause for suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to timely return client funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent failed to timely return client funds when required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The state-court findings included an allegation that respondent failed to timely return client funds; this is cited in the USPTO notice of suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to maintain required trust account books and records
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent failed to maintain the required trust account books and records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The lack of required trust accounting records was cited by the Minnesota Supreme Court and recited in the USPTO disciplinary notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creating shortages in a trust account
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent created shortages in her trust account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Minnesota Supreme Court found that respondent created shortages in her trust account; the USPTO relied on that finding in imposing reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to cooperate with a disciplinary investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent failed to cooperate with a disciplinary investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noncooperation with the disciplinary investigation was among the findings supporting the state suspension and the USPTO's reciprocal action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violations of specified Rules on Lawyers Professional Responsibility (Minnesota rules cited)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Minnesota Supreme Court found respondent admitted to violating multiple rules: Minnesota Rules of Professional Conduct l.4(a)(3), l.4(a)(4), l.15(a), l.15(c)(3), l.15(h), l.16(d), 8.1(b), 8.4(c), and Rule 25 of the Rules on Lawyers Professional Responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order recites the specific rule citations as the predicate violations for the state suspension; these rule violations serve as the factual/legal basis for the USPTO's reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate reciprocal sanction: suspension for 60 days followed by two years' probation upon reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office determined suspension from practice before the USPTO in trademark and other non-patent matters for sixty (60) days followed by probation for two (2) years upon reinstatement is the appropriate discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The suspension is effective the date of the Final Order; the Notice of Suspension to be published recites the same sanction and the factual bases for it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Notice in the Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the Notice of Suspension in the Official Gazette describing the suspension and the reasons for it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order includes the exact Notice language to be published and references availability of disciplinary decisions in the OED FOIA Reading Room.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification to state disciplinary agencies and courts (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director is required to give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the states where the respondent is admitted, to courts where respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order directs the OED Director to provide these notices as part of the disciplinary process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to comply with duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order affirmatively requires compliance with the post-discipline duties set forth in § 11.58 (though the Order does not recite those duties in full).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation from USPTO Customer Numbers and PKI certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO shall dissociate respondent's name from any Customer Numbers and the public key infrastructure (PKI) certificate associated with those Customer Numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This administrative action severs respondent's association with USPTO electronic credentials as part of the discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on obtaining or being added to a USPTO Customer Number until reinstated
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not apply for, obtain, or have her name added to a USPTO Customer Number unless and until she is reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order explicitly bars respondent from USPTO Customer Number access during the suspension/probationary period until reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference to statutory authority: 35 U.S.C. § 32
rubrics_metrics.description: This action is taken pursuant to the provisions of 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order cites 35 U.S.C. § 32 as the statutory authority for USPTO disciplinary actions and publication of discipline.
